uhhamuwa/bring-ram.original: 2? UDU.NÍTA u-un-ni-ia-an-zi nu SÍG ZA.GÌN SÍG SA₅

uhhamuwa/twist-wool.original: 2? UDU.NÍTA u-un-ni-ia-an-zi nu SÍG ZA.GÌN SÍG SA₅
uhhamuwa/twist-wool.english: They twist together blue wool, red wool, yellow(-green) wool, black wool and white wool

uhhamuwa/lead-to-road.original: ḫar-ša-na-la-an-zi nu 1 UDU.NÍTA A-NA KASKAL LÚKÚR pa-ra-a
uhhamuwa/lead-to-road.english: They drive the one ram out onto the road of the enemy

uhhamuwa/appeal-over-ram.english: we have driven [this] crowned ram to you, the god, [for pe]ace.

uhhamuwa/drive-away-ram.english: they drive the one crowned ram away [into] the enemy land.

uhhamuwa/bring-fodder-fat.original: nu EGIR-an-da A-NA ANŠE.KUR.RAMEŠ DINGIR-LIM ŠÀ.GAL.ḪI.A
uhhamuwa/bring-fodder-fat.english: they bring fodder and tallow for the god's horses

uhhamuwa/address-horses-chariot.english: let them eat this fodder and be sated. And let your chariot be greased with tallow.

uhhamuwa/bring-goat-sheep.english: they drive up one billy goat (and) two sheep

uhhamuwa/dedicate-goat.original: nu-kán MÁŠ.GAL DIMIN.IMIN.BI ši-pa-an-ti 1 UDU-ma-kán DUTU-i
uhhamuwa/dedicate-goat.english: He offers the billy goat to the Seven (Sebettu)

uhhamuwa/dedicate-sheep.original: nu-kán MÁŠ.GAL DIMIN.IMIN.BI ši-pa-an-ti 1 UDU-ma-kán DUTU-i
uhhamuwa/dedicate-sheep.english: one sheep he offers to the Sun-god

uhhamuwa/kill-sheep.english: one sheep they kill and cook

uhhamuwa/bring-food-drink.original: nam-ma 1 GA.KIN.AG 1 EM-ṢÚ 1 DUGpu-ul-la-an NINDA EM-ṢÚ
uhhamuwa/bring-food-drink.english: Then they bring one cheese, one sour (loaf), one pulla-vessel of sour bread, one bowl of wine, one bowl of beer and fruit

uhhamuwa/prepare-for-road-god.original: na-at A-NA DINGIR-LIM ŠA KASKAL-NIM i-ia-an-zi
uhhamuwa/prepare-for-road-god.english: they prepare them for the god of the road.

allii/arrange-figures.original: … … … ALAM IM ŠÀ.BA 2 LÚ nu KUŠkur-ša-aš … … … … … …
allii/arrange-figures.english: a [fig]ure of clay; among them two men(?), and a [kur]ša-bag (of leather)

allii/arrange-figures.original: 5 ALAM IM ŠÀ.BA 2 LÚMEŠ nu kur-šu-uš kar-pa-an ḫar-kán-zi
a-ni-ia-mi … ALAM IM ŠÀ.BA 2 LÚ nu KUŠkur-šu-uš kar-pa-an ḫar-kán-zi

allii/seat-patient.original: ḫa-a-an-da-a-ez-zi nu UN-aš ku-iš UḪ₇-an-za na-aš-za DUTU-i me-na-aḫ-ḫa-an-da
allii/seat-patient.english: The person who is bewitched sits down facing the Sun-god

allii/seat-patient.original: nu-za an-tu-wa-aḫ-ḫa-aš ku-iš al-wa-an-za-aḫ-ḫa-an-za na-aš-za DUTU-i

allii/raise-vessel.original: e-ša-ri nu-za MUNUSŠU.GI DUGNA-AK-TA-MA QA-DU ALAM IM da-a-i
allii/raise-vessel.english: the Old Woman takes the naktamu-vessel together with the clay figure and holds it up towards the Sun-god.

allii/raise-vessel.original: nu MUNUSŠU.GI 1 DUGNA-AK-TA-MA QA-DU ALAMḪI.A DUTU-i me-na-aḫ-ḫa-an-da

allii/return-address.original: nu MUNUSŠU.GI ki-iš-ša-an me-ma-i ki-iš-še-ra-aš DUTU-uš ka-a-ša
allii/return-address.english: Let him (the sorcerer) take it back for himself

allii/return-address.original: e-ep-zi MUNUSŠU.GI ki-iš-ša-an me-ma-i ki-iš-ša-ra-aš DUTU-uš

allii/wind-wool.original: nu-uš-ša-an? MUNUSŠU.GI UN-ši ge-nu-wa-aš-ša-aš SÍG da-an-ku-in da-a-i
allii/wind-wool.english: She winds the thread (kapina-) around the figures.

allii/wind-wool.original: EGIR-ŠÚ ŠA SÍG BABBAR ka-pí-na-an QA-TAM-MA i-ia-zi nu te-ez-zi

allii/set-basket.original: nu-uš-ša-an kar-aš ḫal-ki-in NINDApa-aš-šu-uš GIŠPAN 3 GIŠGIḪI.A
allii/set-basket.english: She places kar(a)š-wheat, grain, paššu-breads, a [bow] (and) [three arrows] into a basket and [puts] it be[neath] the bed

allii/set-basket.original: nu-uš-ša-an kar-aš ḫal-ki-in te-pu NINDApa-aš-šu-uš GIŠPAN 3 GIŠGIḪI.A
1 DUGDÍLIM.GAL MUŠEN QA-DU ALAMMEŠ ŠA DUḪ.LÀL GIŠ.NÁ-aš

allii/sleep-over.original: pád-da-ni an-da da-a-i na-at GIŠ.NÁ-aš kat-ta-an da-a-i na-at-ši kat-ta-an še-eš-zi
1 DUGDÍLIM.GAL MUŠEN QA-DU ALAMMEŠ ŠA DUḪ.LÀL GIŠ.NÁ-aš

allii/lift-at-dawn.original: I-NA UD 2KAM ma-a-an lu-uk-kat-ta nu pát-tar GIŠ.NÁ-az kat-ta-an
allii/lift-at-dawn.english: she takes the basket away from be[neath] the bed and swings it away over the person

allii/lift-at-dawn.original: I-NA UD 2KAM ma-a-an lu-uk-kat-ta nu pát-tar GIŠ.NÁ-az kat-ta-an
ma-a-an lu-kat-ta nu DUGDÍLIM.GAL MUŠEN kat-ta-an …

allii/press-earth.original: nu-za ŠA GIŠLAM.ḪAL SAḪARḪI.A-aš da-a-lu-up-pa-an da-a-i?
allii/press-earth.english: She [takes] for herself a clod of earth of the LAM.ḪAL-tree(?), keeps pressing [it] on him

allii/press-dough.original: EGIR-an-da iš-ša!-na-aš da-a-lu-up-pí-in? da-a!-i! na-an-ši-kán an-da
allii/press-dough.english: she takes a l[ump](?) of dough, keeps pressing it on him

ashella/prepare-ram.original: nu ki-i da-aḫ-ḫi ma-aḫ-ḫa-an UDKAM-az ne-ku-uz
ashella/prepare-ram.english: each one prepares a ram for himself

ashella/twist-wool.english: I twist together a cord of white wool, red wool (and) green wool

ashella/twist-wool.original: me-e-ḫu-e-ni DÙ-ri nu ku-e-eš ku-i-e-eš ENMEŠ
ashella/twist-wool.english: I twist together a cord of white wool, red wool and green wool

ashella/bind-ram.original: SÍG SA₅ SÍG SIG₇.SIG₇ an-da tar-na-aḫ-ḫi na-at 1-an an-da
ashella/bind-ram.english: I set into it one [bead(?) and one] ring of iron and of lead, and I bind it onto the necks and horns of the rams.
I set into it one bead and one ring of lead, and I bind it on the necks and horns of the rams.

ashella/tether-ram.original: ŠA A.GAR₅-ia an-da ne-eḫ-ḫi na-at-kán A-NA UDU.ŠIRḪI.A UZUGÚ-ŠU-NU
ashella/tether-ram.english: At night they tie them up in front of the tents
At night they tie them up in front of the tents

ashella/appeal.english: I have tied up these rams; be appeased!

ashella/release-rams.original: nam-ma-kán UDU.ŠIRḪI.A MUNUS-an NINDA.GUR₄.RA KAŠ-ia A-NA KARAŠ
ashella/release-rams.english: They go and let them loose into the enemy's border(-land)
They go and let them run off into the enemy's border(-land)

ashella/slaughter-ram.original: I-NA UD 2KAM ma-a-an lu-uk-kat-ta ka-ru-ú-wa-ri-u-ar ḫu-u-da-ak
ashella/slaughter-ram.english: they slaughter them on the ground

ashella/cook-meat.original: I-NA UD 2KAM ma-a-an lu-uk-kat-ta ka-ru-ú-wa-ri-u-ar ḫu-u-da-ak

ashella/wash-salt-water.english: they pour salt into water and wash their hands with it.

ashella/pass-between-fires.english: they kindle fire in two places and walk out between them.

ashella/offer-goats.original: I-NA UD 2KAM ma-a-an lu-uk-kat-ta ka-ru-ú-wa-ri-u-ar ḫu-u-da-ak
ashella/offer-goats.english: he offers the two billy goats to the Tutelary Deity
he offers the two billy goats to the Tutelary Deity

ashella/bring-pig.english: they quickly drive up one billy goat, one [r]am and one pig
they quickly drive up one billy goat, one sheep and one pig

ashella/offer-pig.english: They offer the billy goat, the ram and the pig to [that] god
they offer the billy goat, the sheep and the pig to that god

ashella/offer-bull.english: He offers the bull to the Storm-god,
They offer the bull to the Storm-god

ashella/offer-ewe.original: UDU.SÍG+MUNUS-ma-kán A-NA DUTU ši-pa-an-ti 3 UDU-ma-kán ḫu-u-ma-an-da-aš
ashella/offer-ewe.english: he offers the ewe to the Sun-god

ashella/offer-rams.original: UDU.SÍG+MUNUS-ma-kán A-NA DUTU ši-pa-an-ti 3 UDU-ma-kán ḫu-u-ma-an-da-aš
ashella/offer-rams.english: they offer the three sheep to all the gods.
the three sheep to all the gods.

pulisa/select-substitutes.original: ma-aḫ-ḫa-an na-aš-kán IŠ-TU ZAG KUR LÚKÚR ar-ḫa i-ia-at-ta-ri
pulisa/select-substitutes.english: they seize one prisoner of war and one woman of the land

pulisa/remove-king-garments.english: (The king) takes the festive garments off his body

pulisa/dress-man.original: 1 MUNUS-TUM-ia pé-ra-an ú-e-da-an-zi nu-za-kán NÍ.TE-ŠU TÚGNÍG.LÁMMEŠ
pulisa/dress-man.english: they clothe the man in them

pulisa/dress-woman.original: 1 MUNUS-TUM-ia pé-ra-an ú-e-da-an-zi nu-za-kán NÍ.TE-ŠU TÚGNÍG.LÁMMEŠ
pulisa/dress-woman.english: the woman they clothe in the festive garments of a woman

pulisa/address-man.original: ar-ḫa da-a-i na-at A-NA LÚ wa-aš-ši-ia-an-zi A-NA MUNUS-TI-ma
pulisa/address-man.english: I have given him an adorned man as his substitute

pulisa/address-woman.original: A-NA MUNUŠ-TI-ma-kán an-da ŠA DINGIR MUNUS-TI me-ma-i -ma QA-TAM-MA-pát
pulisa/address-woman.english: But to the woman he speaks (the words) about a female deity

pulisa/bring-bull-ewe.original: EGIR-an-ta-ma 1 GU₄.MAḪ 1 UDU.ÁŠ.MUNUS.GÀR-ia u-un-na-an-zi nu ŠA KUR LÚKÚR-pát
pulisa/bring-bull-ewe.english: they drive up one bull and one [ewe] of the enemy land itself

pulisa/ring-bull.english: fitted with ašuša-(rings?) at his ears

pulisa/draw-wool.original: SÍG SA₅ SÍG SIG₇.SIG₇ SÍG GE₆ SÍG BABBAR A-NA LUGAL
pulisa/draw-wool.english: Red wool, green wool, black wool (and) [white wool] he draws out of the king's mouth

pulisa/address-bull.original: nu kiš-an me-ma-i ku-iš-wa DINGIR-LUM ku-u-ru-ra-aš ki-i ÚŠ-an DÙ-at
pulisa/address-bull.english: I have given you an [adorned], ašuša-(ringed), approved(?) [bull]

pulisa/address-ewe.english: Afterwards (they bring) the adorned ewe, and he speaks (the words) about a female deity

pulisa/send-animals-ahead.original: nam-ma GU₄.MAḪ a-šu-ša-an-ta-an UDU.ÁŠ.MUNUS.GÀR-ia A-NA LÚŠU.DAB
pulisa/send-animals-ahead.english: they drive the ašuša-(ringed) bull [and the ewe] ahead of [the prisoner] and the woman

tunnawiya/prepare-black-animals.original: ma-a-an LÚ-aš nu UDU.ŠIR GE₆ da-an-zi ma-a-an MUNUS-za-ma nu UDU.SÍG+MUNUS GE₆
tunnawiya/prepare-black-animals.english: If (it is) a man, they take a black ram; but if (it is) a woman, they take a black ewe. (Also) one black piglet

tunnawiya/set-out-black-clothes.original: ma-a-an LÚ-aš nu UDU.ŠIR GE₆ da-an-zi ma-a-an MUNUS-za-ma nu UDU.SÍG+MUNUS GE₆
tunnawiya/set-out-black-clothes.english: One black shirt, one black išḫiyal-

tunnawiya/offer-at-riverbank.original: na-aš ma-aḫ-ḫa-an wa-ap-pu-i a-ri nu 1 NINDA.SIG wa-ap-pu-wa-aš DINGIR.MAḪ pár-ši-ia
tunnawiya/offer-at-riverbank.english: she breaks one thin bread for the Mother-goddess of the riverbank

tunnawiya/address-riverbank-goddess.original: wa-ap-pu-wa-aš DINGIR.MAḪ-aš ka-a-ša EGIR-pa tu-uk ú-wa-nu-un nu-kán ka-a-aš IM-aš

tunnawiya/collect-river-clay.original: wa-ap-pu-wa-aš DINGIR.MAḪ-aš ka-a-ša EGIR-pa tu-uk ú-wa-nu-un nu-kán ka-a-aš IM-aš
tunnawiya/collect-river-clay.english: Then she takes clay of the riverbank.

tunnawiya/offer-at-spring.original: wa-ap-pu-wa-aš DINGIR.MAḪ-aš ka-a-ša EGIR-pa tu-uk ú-wa-nu-un nu-kán ka-a-aš IM-aš
tunnawiya/offer-at-spring.english: she goes to the spring (šakuni-), breaks one thin bread

tunnawiya/collect-spring-clay.original: zi-ik-kán ma-aḫ-ḫa-an ša-ku-〈ni〉-iš GE₆-az KI-az pu-u-ru-ut EGIR ša-ra-a
tunnawiya/collect-spring-clay.english: Then she takes clay of the spring.

tunnawiya/build-reed-hut.original: zi-ik-kán ma-aḫ-ḫa-an ša-ku-〈ni〉-iš GE₆-az KI-az pu-u-ru-ut EGIR ša-ra-a
tunnawiya/build-reed-hut.english: reed huts have meanwhile(?) already been made in front of the river

tunnawiya/make-clay-figures.original: MUNUSŠU.GI wa-ap-pu-wa-aš IM-an ša-ku-ni-ia-aš-ša IM-an a-pí-ia pé-e-da-i

tunnawiya/dress-in-black.original: 1 GU₄ÁB u-ša-an-ta-ri-iš ma-a-an LÚ-aš-ma nu GU₄.MAḪ ḫa-an-da-ez-zi

tunnawiya/hold-black-sheep.original: tu-e-ek-ka₄-aš ša-ra-a pé-eš-še-ez-zi nam-ma 1 UDU GE₆ da-a-i na-an-ši-ša-an
tunnawiya/hold-black-sheep.english: she takes one black sheep and holds it over him

tunnawiya/hold-piglet.original: EGIR-an-da-ma-aš-ši-iš-ša-an ŠAḪ.TUR še-er e-ep-zi nu ŠA ŠAḪ.TUR
tunnawiya/hold-piglet.english: she holds a piglet over him

tunnawiya/hold-puppy.original: EGIR-an-da-ma-aš-ši-iš-ša-an ŠAḪ.TUR še-er e-ep-zi nu ŠA ŠAḪ.TUR
tunnawiya/hold-puppy.english: she holds a puppy over him

tunnawiya/hold-clay-tongue.original: EGIR-an-da-ma-aš-ši-iš-ša-an EME IM še-er e-ep-zi nu ŠA EME
tunnawiya/hold-clay-tongue.english: she holds a clay tongue over him

tunnawiya/melt-figures.original: EGIR-ŠU-ma-aš-ši-ša-an ŠA DUḪ.LÀL ŠA UZUÌ.UDU še-e-nu-uš še-er

tunnawiya/wash-hands-wine.original: ma-aḫ-ḫa-an-ma zi-in-na-i na-aš a-ra-i nu-za-kán ŠUḪI.A GEŠTIN-it
tunnawiya/wash-hands-wine.english: he rises and washes his hands with wine.

tunnawiya/remove-coloured-wool.english: she keeps taking blue wool (and) red wool off his body

tunnawiya/strip-black-clothes.original: nam-ma TÚGGÚ.È.A GE₆-TIM ku-e wa-aš-ša-an ḫar-zi
tunnawiya/strip-black-clothes.english: the Old Woman slits it on him from top to bottom.

tunnawiya/comb-down.english: each maidservant — comb him once downwards with a comb.

tunnawiya/release-into-river.english: she afterwards releases into the river.

tunnawiya/burn-small-animals.english: They carry the puppy (and) the piglet to an uncultivated place and burn them [with fi]re.

tunnawiya/pass-through-gate.english: he goes out beneath the alanza-gate

tunnawiya/return-river-offering.original: na-aš wa-ap-pu-i pa-iz-zi nu wa-ap-pu-ú-i 1 NINDA.SIG
tunnawiya/return-river-offering.english: breaks one thin bread at the riverbank

tunnawiya/take-cow-by-horn.original: nam-ma-za-kán GU₄ u-ša-an-ta-ri-in SI e-ep-zi nu me-ma-i
tunnawiya/take-cow-by-horn.english: she takes the fertile(?) cow by the horn

tunnawiya/wish-for-offspring.original: nam-ma-za-kán GU₄ u-ša-an-ta-ri-in SI e-ep-zi nu me-ma-i
tunnawiya/wish-for-offspring.english: let the ritual patron likewise be fertile

tunnawiya/touch-fruit-tree.english: she goes there and takes hold of it

tunnawiya/wish-by-tree.english: so let the ritual patron likewise be clothed

tunnawiya/libate-sun-god.english: libates to the Sun-god and speaks
